questions.prompt: What is a conceptual data model, as this course's data-modeling framework defines it?
options: A platform-independent description of the real-world entities and relationships a business cares about, with no fields or software named
The Salesforce objects, fields, and relationship types that implement a business requirement
A database schema diagram showing primary keys and foreign keys
A list of all validation rules active on an object
questions.explain: The conceptual model is the platform-independent layer, stated in the business's own vocabulary, with no objects or fields named at all — that's deliberately the first of the three layers, not the last.
questions.distractorExplain: Option 1 describes the physical model, not the conceptual model. The physical layer is where Salesforce-specific objects and relationship types actually get decided, and that's deliberately the last of the three layers this course teaches, not the first.

questions.prompt: A requirements conversation starts with a stakeholder saying 'so we'd need a new field called Preferred_Contact_Method__c.' Per this course's conceptual/logical/physical framework, what has likely gone wrong?
options: Nothing — starting with a field name is the correct way to begin any requirements conversation
The field name is invalid because it doesn't end in the correct suffix
The stakeholder has jumped to the physical layer before the conceptual and logical layers have been agreed on, risking a model that locks in a first guess at the business concept
This automatically means the object must be a junction object
questions.explain: Starting at the physical layer before the business has agreed on the conceptual model is the most common architect mistake this lesson warns about — it risks permanently encoding a first guess into object and field names that are expensive to rename later.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a roll-up summary field can perform COUNT, SUM, MIN, and ________ calculations, but has no native AVERAGE option.
questions.explain: Roll-up summary fields support exactly four calculation types — COUNT, SUM, MIN, and MAX — with no native AVERAGE, per Salesforce's own documentation on roll-up summary mechanics.

questions.prompt: Match each Salesforce relationship concept to what it actually does.
right: A special lookup type available only on the User object, used for management chains
A loose, optional link with no effect on deletion or security
A tight link where the detail record's existence, ownership, and sharing are controlled by its master
A custom object with two relationship fields used to model a many-to-many relationship
questions.explain: Lookup is the loose, optional link with no effect on deletion or security. Master-detail is the tight link controlling the detail's existence, ownership, and sharing. A junction object (two relationship fields) is how many-to-many is modeled. Hierarchical relationships are the special User-object-only lookup used for management chains.

questions.prompt: Why can a person account never have a second, separate Contact the way a business Account can have many?
options: Because person accounts don't support Contacts at all
Because person accounts automatically convert any extra Contact into a child Account
Because Contacts are deprecated on person accounts
Because the person contact created with a person account is uniquely bound to it and is the only contact record that can be associated directly with that person account
questions.explain: Per Salesforce's own SOAP API documentation, the person contact created alongside a person account is uniquely bound to it — it's the only contact record that can be associated directly with the person account, unlike a business Account which can have many separate Contacts.

questions.prompt: Select every statement that correctly describes something a master-detail relationship controls that a lookup relationship does not.
options: Deleting the master record cascades to delete its detail records
The detail record's Owner field is unavailable and is automatically set to the master's owner
The master-detail field is required on the detail record's page layout
The detail record can have its own independent sharing rules and queues
By default, a detail record's master cannot be changed once set (reparenting is restricted)
questions.explain: Master-detail controls cascade delete, forces ownership/sharing inheritance from the master, requires the relationship field on the layout, and restricts reparenting by default. A detail record having its own independent sharing and queues is exactly what a lookup allows and master-detail does not — detail records have no independent Owner field at all.

questions.prompt: Put these three data-modeling altitudes in the order this course teaches them, from least to most platform-specific.
items: Conceptual model — real-world entities and relationships, no software named
Logical model — typed entities, attributes, and business rules, still platform-independent
Physical model — the logical model implemented in Salesforce's specific objects, fields, and relationship mechanics
questions.explain: The discipline runs conceptual to logical to physical: agree on the business concept in plain language first, structure it into typed entities and rules second, and only then decide the Salesforce-specific implementation — keeping each layer a cheap checkpoint instead of an expensive change request after go-live.

questions.prompt: An Account has a Total_Open_Opportunity_Value__c field that is kept in sync automatically by a Flow whenever a related Opportunity changes. What is this an example of?
options: A normalization violation that should never be allowed in Salesforce
A native roll-up summary field
A deliberate denormalization, which is a legitimate architectural tool as long as something reliable keeps the duplicated value in sync
A Big Object
questions.explain: This is denormalization done deliberately through custom automation rather than a native roll-up summary field (which requires a master-detail relationship) — a legitimate pattern as long as the Flow reliably keeps the duplicated value in sync.

questions.prompt: A custom object has 5 fields; another has 200 fields, including large text areas. Both are ordinary custom objects with no documented exceptions. What does this course's storage lesson say about their per-record storage cost?
options: The 200-field object costs roughly 40 times more storage per record
Only the object with large text areas counts against storage at all
Field count has no relationship to storage cost for any object type, without exception
Most records count toward data storage at a small, fixed amount regardless of field count, so the two objects generally cost about the same per record
questions.explain: The lesson's core point is that record count, not field count, drives storage cost for the vast majority of standard and custom object records — a handful of documented exceptions exist (like Campaigns and email-related records), but the general rule is that width barely matters compared to row volume.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a custom Big Object's API name always ends in ________.
questions.explain: Custom Big Objects are metadata-defined objects whose API names always end in __b, distinguishing them from standard objects and ordinary custom objects (__c).

questions.prompt: Match each dataset placement mechanism to the situation it fits best.
right: Configuration an admin should be able to tune live, directly in production, without a deployment
Data generated inside Salesforce in very large volume, rarely edited, queried mainly through a defined index
Configuration that should be identical across environments and deployed like code
Data owned and maintained in an outside system, accessed live without storing a copy
questions.explain: A Big Object fits very large, rarely-edited, Salesforce-generated data queried through its index. An External Object fits data owned elsewhere, accessed live via Salesforce Connect. A Custom Metadata Type fits configuration deployed like code, identical across environments. A Custom Setting fits configuration an admin tunes live in production without a deployment.

questions.prompt: Per Salesforce's own large-data-volume guidance cited in this course, roughly what concentration of child records under a single parent Account is the point where skew-related problems typically start to show up?
options: More than 100 child records under one parent
More than 1 million child records under one parent
Skew only matters above 1 billion records, regardless of concentration
More than 10,000 child records under one parent
questions.explain: Salesforce's own large-data-volume guidance treats more than 10,000 child records under the same parent as the point where record locking and sharing recalculation typically start becoming measurably more expensive.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about bulkification and performance at scale, per this course.
options: Automation that issues one SOQL query or DML statement per record inside a loop will hit governor limits once enough records pass through it at once
Code that performs fine in a sandbox with a handful of test records is guaranteed to perform fine in production at full data volume
Batch Apex and Queueable Apex exist specifically to chunk large volumes into governor-limit-safe pieces
A role-hierarchy change on a large, skewed object can trigger an expensive, org-wide sharing recalculation
Query selectivity against indexed fields matters equally regardless of how many records an object holds
questions.explain: Unbulkified per-record loops hit governor limits at volume even though they pass small-scale tests. Batch/Queueable Apex exist to chunk large jobs safely. A role change on a skewed object can trigger a costly sharing recalculation. Selectivity matters far more as record count grows — it does not matter 'equally' regardless of volume, and passing a small-scale test is never a guarantee of production performance.

questions.prompt: What is data skew, as this course defines it?
options: A field whose values are stored in the wrong data type
Excessive concentration of records against a single parent, owner, or lookup target, rather than those records spreading out
A report that returns an incorrect total due to a formula error
The total number of records stored in an org, regardless of how they are distributed
questions.explain: Data skew specifically means concentration — too many records tied to one parent, one owner, or one lookup target — not raw volume. A million-record object isn't automatically a problem; skew is about how those records are distributed.
questions.distractorExplain: The option describing total record count regardless of distribution describes raw volume, not skew. This course is explicit that a million-record object isn't automatically a problem — skew is specifically about concentration around a single parent, owner, or lookup target, not the total number of records in the org.

questions.prompt: Put these four steps of building a storage forecast in the order this course teaches them.
items: Baseline current usage by object from the Storage Usage page
Identify which integrations or automations are the growth drivers, and at what rate
Project usage forward against the org's current allocation
Decide the relief valve, such as an archiving or purge policy, before the limit is actually reached
questions.explain: The forecasting discipline runs baseline, then identify drivers, then project forward, then decide the relief valve in advance — turning a storage-limit breach from a surprise into a planned, deliberate decision made before the org is under time pressure.

questions.prompt: In a RACI matrix governing data ownership for the Account object, why must 'Accountable' be assigned to a single named role rather than a committee?
options: Because Salesforce technically prevents more than one approver per object
Because 'Accountable' and 'Responsible' must always be the same role
So that when two departments disagree about a change, there is one role whose call is final after consulting both sides, rather than a stalemate
Because committees are not allowed to be 'Consulted' in a RACI matrix
questions.explain: The critical property of a RACI model is that Accountable is a single name, not a committee — when two departments disagree, that one role makes the final call after consulting both sides, instead of the dispute being resolved by whoever escalates loudest.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: instead of 'golden record,' Salesforce's Data Cloud identity-resolution documentation describes its Unified Profile output as a system of ________.
questions.explain: Salesforce's Data Cloud documentation deliberately avoids 'golden record' language, describing its Unified Profile as a 'system of reference' because it links source profiles together under match rules rather than overwriting or replacing them.

questions.prompt: Match each data-governance role to what it is actually accountable for.
right: The role accountable for a business process that touches the data, without owning the data itself
The role performing the day-to-day work of keeping data correct, such as resolving duplicates
The business-side role accountable for a dataset's accuracy and approving structural changes
The role accountable for the platform itself — uptime, licensing, release management
questions.explain: The data owner is the business-side role accountable for accuracy and approving structural changes. The data steward does the day-to-day work of keeping data correct. The system owner is accountable for the platform itself, not the data's quality. The business process owner is accountable for a process touching the data, without owning the data itself.

questions.prompt: A sales rep views an account's invoice balance inside Salesforce, where it was synced in from the ERP. What is Salesforce acting as in this specific data domain, per this course's distinction?
options: The system of record for the invoice balance, since the rep sees it there first
A system of engagement displaying a copy, not the system of record for that financial data
A Big Object
A master data management hub
questions.explain: Even though the rep lives in Salesforce all day, the ERP remains the system of record for the invoice balance — Salesforce here is only the system of engagement displaying a synced copy, which is exactly the conflation this course's Lesson 17 warns against.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about the three kinds of metadata this course distinguishes.
options: Technical metadata describes a field's structural definition, such as its data type and relationships
Business metadata describes what a field means in business terms, such as its intended definition and acceptable use
Operational metadata describes how data behaves in practice, such as which job refreshes it and how often
Salesforce's Object Manager and Schema Builder alone provide complete coverage of all three metadata categories
A field can have excellent technical metadata while having no business or operational metadata documented at all
questions.explain: Technical, business, and operational metadata are three genuinely different categories. Object Manager and Schema Builder only provide accurate technical metadata — they say nothing about business meaning or operational behavior, which is exactly why a field can have excellent technical metadata and none of the other two.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between what Field History Tracking captures and what Setup Audit Trail captures?
options: They capture exactly the same information, just in different user interfaces
Setup Audit Trail tracks data value changes, while Field History Tracking tracks configuration changes
Both tools retain their history indefinitely with no retention window
Field History Tracking logs changes to data values on tracked fields; Setup Audit Trail logs changes to metadata and configuration in Setup — neither captures the other's category
questions.explain: Field History Tracking is a data-value-change log (with a limited retention window); Setup Audit Trail is a metadata/configuration-change log covering roughly the last 180 days. Neither one, by itself, gives full data lineage, and neither covers what the other tracks.

questions.prompt: Put these three master data management steps in the order they occur when reconciling the same customer across multiple systems.
items: Match rules decide whether two records from different systems describe the same real-world entity
Survivorship rules decide, once records are matched, which field values win
The resulting trusted version (or linked Unified Profile) is made available for every system to reference
questions.explain: MDM mechanics run match first (are these the same entity), then survivorship (which values win once matched), and only then is the resulting trusted or linked record made available enterprise-wide.

questions.prompt: A company's business units genuinely operate as one integrated supply chain, sharing the same Account and Order concepts everywhere. Per this course's framework, what does this fact argue for?
options: A multi-org strategy, since integrated businesses always need isolation
Immediately enabling person accounts
A single-org strategy, since standardization and one shared schema benefit a genuinely integrated business
Converting all Accounts into Big Objects
questions.explain: A single-org strategy's main draw is exactly this situation: when a business genuinely operates as one integrated company, a single shared schema gives standardization and simple cross-business reporting that multiple orgs would fragment.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: per the official Apex governor limits this course cites, a synchronous Apex transaction can issue up to ________ SOQL queries.
questions.explain: A synchronous Apex transaction can issue up to 100 SOQL queries (200 for asynchronous Apex), per Salesforce's official Execution Governors and Limits documentation cited in the Scalability Considerations lesson.

questions.prompt: Match each multi-business-unit data architecture technique to what it does.
right: Controls record-level visibility between business units without separating the schema or the org
Holds detail that has no analog in any other business unit, related back to the shared core object
Lets one object carry different layouts, picklists, and required fields per business unit while the schema stays unified
Identifies which business unit a shared record belongs to, making it queryable and reportable
questions.explain: Record types let one object carry different layouts/picklists per business unit on a unified schema. A Business Unit field makes 'which unit owns this' queryable. A business-unit-specific child object holds detail with no analog elsewhere. Sharing rules and role hierarchy control record-level visibility without separating the schema or the org.

questions.prompt: In the Halvorsen Industrial Supply case study, why was a lookup relationship chosen over master-detail from Order to Account?
options: Master-detail relationships cannot be created on custom objects
Orders didn't need to inherit Account's sharing or be deleted when the Account is deleted, and master-detail risked concentrating skew on Halvorsen's largest distributor accounts
Lookup relationships are always required for any object with more than 1 million records
Halvorsen wanted a native roll-up summary field placed directly on Order
questions.explain: The architect's reasoning combined two things: Orders didn't need master-detail's cascade-delete or sharing-inheritance behavior, and with 60 million Orders against 11 million Accounts, master-detail risked concentrating parent-account skew on Halvorsen's largest distributor accounts.

questions.prompt: In the Carrow Mutual Wealth Advisory case study, select every true statement about how systems of record were assigned.
options: The core banking platform remained the system of record for account balances, holdings, and transactions
Salesforce became the system of record for advisor relationship data, suitability assessments, and compliance sign-offs
Balance data was replicated into a custom Salesforce object to give advisors faster access
External Objects via Salesforce Connect were used to surface live balance data without storing a copy in Salesforce
Client identity data was assigned its own separate master-data decision, distinct from the balance/transaction system-of-record decision
questions.explain: The core banking platform stayed authoritative for balances/transactions; Salesforce became system of record for relationship and compliance data; External Objects surfaced live balance data without replication; and client identity got its own distinct master-data decision. Replicating balance data into a custom object is exactly what the case study's architect avoided, since it would have created the authoritative-copy risk the systems-of-record decision was designed to prevent.

questions.prompt: A data model review finds two custom objects that were independently built by two different teams to capture nearly the same concept. Which review category does this fall under?
options: Duplicate or overlapping objects
Automation load
Relationship health
Classification and ownership drift
questions.explain: Two independently-grown objects capturing nearly the same concept is the textbook duplicate/overlapping-objects finding — a consolidation opportunity a structured data model review is specifically designed to surface.

questions.prompt: Put these four decisions from the Halvorsen Industrial Supply case study in the order the lesson applies them.
items: Decide whether single-org or multi-org fits the business
Choose lookup vs. master-detail for Order-to-Account and check for skew risk
Decide an archiving cutoff for old closed Orders
Write up the recommendation, tying each decision to a specific business requirement
questions.explain: The case study applies the course's concepts in order: first the org-strategy decision, then relationship design and skew avoidance, then storage and archiving strategy, and finally a write-up tying every decision back to one of Halvorsen's actual numbers or constraints.

questions.prompt: Why does an architecture decision record (ADR) capture something a data dictionary and a Schema Builder diagram cannot?
options: An ADR updates itself automatically whenever the schema changes
A data dictionary and Schema Builder diagram already capture decision reasoning, making ADRs redundant
An ADR records the reasoning, alternatives considered, and tradeoff behind a decision, not just the resulting structure or field meaning
ADRs are generated automatically by the Metadata API
questions.explain: A data dictionary tells you what a field means, and Schema Builder shows structure — neither captures why a specific decision was made or what alternatives were weighed. An ADR transfers that judgment, which is exactly what a successor needs to extend the system well instead of undoing a load-bearing decision by accident.
